title: How Does a Cat Purr? Vocal Cords That Work Without a Brain
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. It explains how a cat's purr is produced. For decades the accepted explanation was that the brain contracts and relaxes the laryngeal muscles twenty-five to thirty times a second. A two thousand twenty-three study in Current Biology produced sound at purring frequency from excised cat larynges with nothing but blown air and no nerve signal.
